title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): G = GL_2 over a base (sections over a site/scheme T or S), PG = PGL_2, SG = SL_2. A regular element ρ of G has the class function Δ(ρ) = (Tr ρ)^2 / det ρ, which descends to PG. On the previous page Grothendieck proves that two regular sections ρ̃, ρ̃' of PG are locally conjugate if and only if Δ(ρ̃) = Δ(ρ̃'), at least when Δ(ρ̃) is invertible (equivalently Tr ρ is invertible). The proof first rescales by λ so that det ρ = det ρ'. The equality Tr²ρ' = Tr²ρ then gives a unit ε = Tr ρ'/Tr ρ with ε² = 1. Hence ρ' is locally conjugate to ερ.

Remark on this page: without the invertibility hypothesis the statement fails. (The transcription's 'A_0 non intègre' is almost certainly 'Δ(ρ) non inv.'.) Take A = A_0[w,w']/(w^2, ww', w'^2), whose augmentation ideal is free of rank 2 on w and w'. Set ρ = [[0,1],[-1,w]] and ρ' = [[0,1],[-1,w']].
- Both are companion matrices, hence regular, with det = 1, Tr = w and w' respectively.
- So (Tr)^2 = 0 for both and Δ(ρ) = Δ(ρ') = 0.
- If ρ' were locally conjugate to λρ for a unit λ = a + bw + cw', then λw = aw. This would have to equal w', which is impossible since w and w' are independent. So Tr ρ and Tr ρ' are not 'homothetic' and the classes in PG differ.

Part 2), 'relative position of two sections ρ, σ of G': the relevant objects are ε̃0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃ and ε̃1 = ρ̃σ̃^{-1} in PG. These are conjugate: ε̃1 = ρ̃ ε̃0 ρ̃^{-1} = σ̃ ε̃0 σ̃^{-1}. Two conditions are imposed.
- 1°: ε̃0 and ε̃1 lift to SL_2, as elements ε0, ε1 related by ε1 = ρ(ε0) = σ(ε0) for suitable representatives. After normalising scalars, ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ and ε1 = -ρσ^{-1}.
- 2°: they are fibrewise unipotent, ε_i = 1 + N_i with N_i nilpotent.

The next page then puts ρ in the normal form [[0,u],[v,w]] adapted to the flag ('épi-gluf') defined by N_0 and N_1. It derives u' = -u, v' = -v and w' = w - u, i.e. ρ + σ = uP with P the elementary projection. So σ is determined by ρ and the flag. This is the algebraic analysis of pairs of elements of PGL_2 whose 'quotients' σ^{-1}ρ and ρσ^{-1} are parabolic (unipotent), in families over arbitrary bases. It presumably serves the study of the 'loop equation' (relations among generators of π1 of punctured spheres / Teichmüller-type groups) represented in PGL_2.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The counterexample is correct: companion matrices are regular, det = 1, Tr² = 0 for both, and no unit λ satisfies λw = w' in A_0[w,w']/(w,w')^2.

Minor point: the hypothesis that fails is invertibility of Δ (Tr ρ), not integrality of the base. The example uses a non-reduced base, but the relevant condition, as stated on the previous page, is Δ invertible.

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of regular elements of PGL_2 over an arbitrary base are classified locally by Δ = Tr²/det when Δ is invertible; counterexample over a nonreduced base when Δ is nilpotent.
ideas.modern_name: Adjoint quotient / Chevalley–Steinberg map for PGL_2 and fibres over non-reduced bases (regular centralizers, Kostant section)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kostant, Steinberg (over fields); over bases: SGA3-era group-scheme theory, later Ngô (regular centralizers)
ideas.where_published: Related general theory in SGA 3; this specific PGL_2 statement and counterexample not known in published form

ideas.what: Pairs of sections ρ, σ of GL_2 with σ^{-1}ρ and ρσ^{-1} (conjugate in PGL_2) required to lift to SL_2 and be fibrewise unipotent; normal form σ = -ρ + uP.
ideas.modern_name: Parabolic (unipotent-monodromy) PGL_2 representations of punctured-sphere groups / normal forms for pairs of elements with parabolic product
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke–Klein trace coordinates; character varieties of punctured spheres)
ideas.where_published: Not published; part of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' following La Longue Marche

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds an elementary counterexample in nilpotent deformations and the setup of a normal-form computation for pairs in PGL_2 with unipotent quotients. Both are routine; the interest is only as part of the unpublished 'équation des lacets' programme.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Rmq Si A_0 [?] non intègre' should likely read 'Rmq Si Δ(ρ) non inv.', referring to the invertibility hypothesis of the previous page.
Line 2 likely reads '(Tr ρ)^2 = 0, (Tr ρ')^2 = 0, det ρ = det ρ' = 1, Tr ρ et Tr ρ' n'étant pas homothétiques' (consistent with the transcription).
The parenthetical after A = A_0[w,w']/(w², ww', w'²) appears to say the augmentation ideal is a free module of rank 2 generated by w and w'.
In (25) the struck-out symbol before σ^{-1}ρ (rendered λ_0) is a cancelled scalar; the final normalisation is ε0 = -σ^{-1}ρ, ε1 = -ρσ^{-1}.
Condition 1° wording ('multiplicités singulières') is uncertain. Context shows it means ε̃0, ε̃1 lift to SG = SL_2 (possibly 'sont unimodulaires/spéciaux').
